concepts.title: Crisis of 1991 and the New Economic Policy LPG

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Crisis of 1991 and the New Economic Policy LPG' refers to.
questions.a: The balance of payments crisis of 1991, with dwindling foreign exchange reserves and heavy external debt, forced India to adopt the New Economic Policy of stabilisation and structural reform in three streams: liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Crisis of 1991 and the New Economic Policy LPG'.
questions.a: Reforms dismantled the licensing raj, opened sectors to private and foreign investment, and integrated India with the world economy.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Crisis of 1991 and the New Economic Policy LPG' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Economic reforms 1991 (source: keec103.txt LPG overview sections)

concepts.title: Liberalisation: Deregulation of Industry, Finance, Trade and Tax

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Liberalisation: Deregulation of Industry, Finance, Trade and Tax' refers to.
questions.a: Liberalisation freed economic activity from state controls by abolishing industrial licensing for most industries, deregulating the financial sector, reducing tariffs and removing quantitative restrictions on imports, and reforming direct and indirect taxes to simplify compliance.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Liberalisation: Deregulation of Industry, Finance, Trade and Tax'.
questions.a: Freedom of production, trade and finance was expected to let market prices allocate resources better than licences and controls.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Liberalisation: Deregulation of Industry, Finance, Trade and Tax' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Privatisation, Globalisation and Demonetisation GST Context

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Privatisation, Globalisation and Demonetisation GST Context' refers to.
questions.a: Privatisation transfers ownership or management from the public to the private sector through disinvestment of equity of public sector undertakings, while globalisation integrates the domestic economy with the world through trade liberalisation, foreign direct investment inflows and outward orientation of policy.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Privatisation, Globalisation and Demonetisation GST Context'.
questions.a: Disinvestment sales of PSU equity aimed to raise resources and improve efficiency, and globalisation opened the economy to foreign competition and technology.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Privatisation, Globalisation and Demonetisation GST Context' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Privatisation and globalisation (source: keec103.txt privatisation globalisation sections)

concepts.title: Appraisal of Reforms: Gains, Critique and Positive Features

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Appraisal of Reforms: Gains, Critique and Positive Features' refers to.
questions.a: Reforms raised growth of the economy and foreign exchange reserves and expanded the service sector, but critics note limited employment growth, neglect of agriculture, uneven industrial growth and greater inequality, while positive assessments emphasise efficiency and consumer gains.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Appraisal of Reforms: Gains, Critique and Positive Features'.
questions.a: The reform appraisal weighs faster GDP growth and reserves against jobless growth and agrarian neglect.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Appraisal of Reforms: Gains, Critique and Positive Features' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Appraisal of reforms (source: keec103.txt appraisal sections)
